svg.title: Three roads: a map of who fits where
svg.desc: Schematic map of the three roads for a small HCC, plus transplantation. Resectable with good liver function — surgical resection remains the default (AASLD 2023, BCLC 2022); up to 2 cm in a needle-reachable position — resection and RFA offer the same survival benefit, and beyond 2 cm resection should be favoured in resectable patients (BCLC 2022); not fit for surgery, not fit for ablation, or firmly declining surgery — the SBRT slot (AASLD: usable for central and perivascular tumours; Taiwan NHI code 37047B, reimbursed since 2015: single lesion up to 5 cm, Child-Pugh A to B, unfit for or failed surgery, embolisation or ablation); a liver that cannot pay (Child-Pugh score 8 or above, uncontrolled ascites or encephalopathy) — avoid external-beam radiotherapy; within the Milan criteria (single tumour up to 5 cm, or up to 3 tumours each up to 3 cm) — transplant assessment must not be skipped, as the only option treating both the cancer and the cirrhosis. The final decision belongs to the multidisciplinary team.

g.text: SIZE × LOCATION × LIVER FUNCTION
Three roads: a map of who fits where
'All feasible' is not 'all the same' — each road has its home ground, plus a fourth: transplant.
Where you land depends on imaging and liver function; the final call belongs to the multidisciplinary team.
Resectable with good liver function — surgical resection remains the default (AASLD 2023 / BCLC 2022)
Resectable · good liver
Surgical resection = the default road
AASLD 2023: the curative treatment of choice for localised HCC without cirrhosis;
BCLC 2022: if transplant and surgery are both options, resection should be the first choice.
'Equal after adjustment' is not 'skipping surgery is the same' — no SBRT-vs-resection trial exists.
Up to 2 cm · needle-reachable
Resection or RFA: the same survival benefit (BCLC 2022)
Beyond 2 cm, complete responses fall and local recurrence rises after ablation —
resection should be favoured in resectable patients (BCLC 2022).
Unfit to operate or ablate
The SBRT slot — real, and large
For those unfit for surgery, unfit for ablation — or firmly declining surgery after hearing all sides.
AASLD 2023: another route to durable local control when thermal ablation is not feasible;
usable for central and perivascular tumours. Taiwan NHI 37047B (reimbursed since 2015):
single lesion ≤5 cm, Child-Pugh A–B, unfit for — or failed — surgery, embolisation or ablation.
A liver that cannot pay
Here SBRT is the wrong answer
AASLD 2023: Child-Pugh 8 or above, uncontrolled ascites or hepatic encephalopathy —
avoid external-beam radiotherapy. Restore the liver first, or assess for transplant.
Within transplant criteria
Transplant assessment must not be skipped
The only option treating the cancer and the cirrhosis together. Milan criteria (single ≤5 cm,
or ≤3 tumours each ≤3 cm): 4-year survival 75%, recurrence-free 83% (1996, 48 patients).
Every local-treatment road runs alongside transplant assessment — it does not replace it.
Read size, location and liver function together; for multinodular, embolisable intermediate-stage disease see the TACE and Y-90 article.
Schematic, redrawn from AASLD 2023, BCLC 2022, the Taiwan NHI 37047B reimbursement criteria (since 2015) and Mazzaferro 1996
Where you land is for the multidisciplinary team to judge
